newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pushed up by futures, turnover low.
newsitem.headline: German shares pushed up by futures, turnover low.

text.p: German shares rose on Thursday against a weaker overnight trend on Wall Street, with dealers putting the gains down to a strong but unexpected gain on the index futures market.
The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade gained 34.91 points, 1.04 percent to 3,401.78 early on. June DAX futures were up 38.5 points to 3,408.5.

"It's mainly down to the rise in futures, which in turn was a bit surprising," said one dealer, adding that a firmer dollar at just under 1.72 marks was also helping trade. Overall share volumes were however relatively thin.

With little corporate news or economic data scheduled, dealers expect trade to be range-bound for the rest of the day. German state inflation data coming through on Thursday morning was seen having little market impact.
Early gainers included Deutsche Bank, up 1.45 marks at 91.18 marks and Siemens AG, which rose 1.40 marks at 89.40.
Viag unit Computer 2000, which does not trade on IBIS, warned that it expected a 1996/97 group net loss and might not pay a dividend.
